# User-defined package

#### Course: Learn Java Intermediate

## User-defined package

Till now we have learned and used built-in packages. For example,

```java
// to take input value
import java.util.Scanner;

// to use the ArrayList class
import java.util.ArrayList;
```

These packages provide methods that we have been using to perform various tasks in our program.

In Java, we can also create custom packages, known as user-defined packages.

Create a Java Package

We use the package keyword to define a package in Java.

```java
package packageName;
```

Java uses file system directories to store packages. Now, let's create a Java file Teacher.java inside another directory.

For example:

![Java package](data:image/png;base64,)

Now, to write code in Teacher.java, we must write the package statement at the beginning of the program.

```java
package programiz;
```

Here, any class that is created inside the programiz directory belongs to the programiz package.

Here's the code:

```java
package programiz;

public class Teacher {
    
    public void getTeacherInfo(int id, String name) {
      
        System.out.println(id);
        System.out.println(name);
    }
}
```

Now, let's create another java file (Student.java) inside the programiz package.

![Java package](data:image/png;base64,)

```java
package programiz;

public class Student {
    
    public void getStudentInfo(int id, String name) {
        
        System.out.println(id);
        System.out.println(name);
    }
}
```
